general_recommendations: Screen for and treat aetiologies and cardiovascular and non-cardiovascular comorbidities in patients with HFpEF.
Diuretics are recommended in congested patients with HF to alleviate symptoms and signs.
prevention_of_chronic_HF: Treat hypertension to prevent or delay onset of HF and to reduce HF hospitalizations.
Use statins in patients at high risk of cardiovascular disease or with established CV disease to prevent or delay onset of HF and reduce HF hospitalizations.

SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with diabetes at high risk of CV disease or with CV disease to prevent HF hospitalizations.
Counsel against sedentary behaviour, obesity, cigarette smoking, and alcohol abuse to prevent or delay HF onset.
management_of_chronic_HF: Enroll HF patients in multidisciplinary HF management programmes to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and mortality.
Recommend self-management strategies and either home-based and/or clinic-based programmes to improve outcomes and reduce HF hospitalization and mortality.
Recommend exercise for all patients able to improve exercise capacity, quality of life, and reduce HF hospitalization.
treatment_of_advanced_HF: Patients considered for long-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) must have good compliance, appropriate capacity for device handling and psychosocial support.
Heart transplantation is recommended for patients with advanced HF refractory to medical/device therapy who do not have absolute contraindications.
treatment_of_acute_HF: Give oxygen if SpO2 < 90% or PaO2 < 60 mmHg to correct hypoxaemia.
Consider intubation for progressive respiratory failure despite oxygen/non-invasive ventilation.
Intravenous loop diuretics are recommended for acute HF with signs/symptoms of fluid overload to improve symptoms.
Thromboprophylaxis (e.g., with LMWH) is recommended in patients not already anticoagulated and with no contraindication, to reduce venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism risk.
Inotropic agents are not routinely recommended due to safety concerns and should be reserved for patients with symptomatic hypotension and evidence of hypoperfusion.
Routine use of opioids is not recommended except in selected patients with severe/intractable pain or anxiety.
Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is not routinely recommended post-MI cardiogenic shock.
post_hospitalization_management: Carefully evaluate patients hospitalized for HF to exclude persistent signs of congestion before discharge and optimize oral treatment.
Start evidence-based oral medical treatment prior to discharge when possible.
Arrange early follow-up (1–2 weeks after discharge) to assess congestion, drug tolerance, and start/uptitrate evidence-based therapy.
HF_and_atrial_fibrillation: Long-term oral anticoagulation recommended in all patients with AF, HF, and CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥2 in men or ≥3 in women.
Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) preferred over VKAs in patients with HF except in those with moderate/severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic valves.
Urgent electrical cardioversion (ECV) recommended for acute worsening of HF with rapid ventricular rates and haemodynamic instability.
Anti-arrhythmic agents such as flecainide, encainide, disopyramide, dronedarone, and D-sotalol are not recommended due to safety concerns.
